items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: the three of us in Jimmy Dorsey’s band, the bassist and the pianist and myself formed a trio, sort of a la Nat Cole

ctx.x: Good, good. Tell us how you got started working with probably one of the greatest trios in all of jazz — Oscar Peterson and Ray Brown.

I was playing, I had been with bands, I’d been with Jimmy Dorsey, and the three of us in Jimmy Dorsey’s band, the bassist and the pianist and myself formed a trio, sort of a la Nat Cole, and we were playing in Buffalo. And we played in the same hotel for, oh months at a time. And the people from Canada, there was no liquor in Canada on Sundays at that time, but they’d come over for the music. And a lot of them came. And one night they brought Oscar Peterson with them. And he sat in and played with us and then…
You know that says something about musicians striking a certain chemistry.
